component.name: NAM-X
component.summary: Play Neural Amp Modeler profiles and impulse responses live

description.p: NAM-X is a standalone guitar rig for Linux and Windows built on Neural Amp Modeler. Load any .nam model and .wav impulse response from the community, play through it live with a few milliseconds of latency, and shape the sound with a freely reorderable effects chain: tuner, transpose, noise gate, compressor, dynamic wah, flanger, phaser, Tube Screamer drive, volume pedal, four-band EQ, chorus, tremolo, stereo delay, reverb and cab simulation.
A library panel keeps models, IRs and presets one click away, with search, favorites and recents. Presets carry the whole rig: every setting, the effect order and the model and IR they use.
Audio goes through JACK or PipeWire on Linux and WASAPI on Windows. NAM-X is an independent project and is not affiliated with the official Neural Amp Modeler plugin.

screenshot.caption: The rack with a Mesa model and a Celestion V30 cabinet loaded

description.p: ASIO on Windows: NAM-X can now use your audio interface's own ASIO driver, beside WASAPI (Settings, Audio, Driver), for the lowest latency.

Native look: NAM-X follows the desktop's widget style (Union/Breeze on Plasma, Windows 11 on Windows) and system font; three theme-switch crashes fixed; the AppImage draws SVG icon themes. Presets leave the Input, Output and limiter alone and keep their tempo when a Sync switch is on; the tempo and tuner reference fields are standard spin boxes.
First public release: reorderable effects chain, library panel, presets, MIDI control, tuner and metronome, JACK/PipeWire and WASAPI backends.
